title: Patch: the first page load stops downloading the whole patch history to read one version number
thread:
**Issue #3499 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3499: Patch: the first page load stops downloading the whole patch history to read one version number
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Every first visit to the site, the landing page included, downloads the full text of every patch note ever shipped, only to read the newest version's name. That is 650 KB, or 106 KB compressed, which is more than the whole card catalog. It grows with every patch: it has nearly quadrupled in a month. Once this is built, the first load fetches only that name and the few facts the "new" ribbon needs. The patch notes page still loads the full history when it is opened.

## Why

- **The import exists only for the version.** `apps/web/src/wire/cards.ts:6` statically imports `crates/cards/patches/patches.json` (650,197 bytes; 106,337 gzipped, against 68,878 for `catalog.json`). It uses it only for `CATALOG_VERSION = newestVersion(patchesJson)` (line 24), the last entry's `version`.
- **The first file the page loads pulls it in.** `apps/web/src/main.tsx:79` imports `NotFoundPlay`. `NotFoundPlay.tsx:8` imports `CATALOG` from `@jackioh/cards`, which is `wire/cards.ts`.
- **A second static import.** `apps/web/src/patches/ribbon.ts:6` imports the same file to work out `NEW_RIBBON_SET`.
- **It undoes the lazy loading.** `apps/web/src/patches/source.ts:164` loads the patch files lazily for the Patch notes page (`import.meta.glob(..., { import: "default" })`). The two static imports above defeat that.
- **It is growing fast:** 170,512 bytes on 2026-10-08, 650,197 today.
- **Nothing checks the size of the first load.** `scripts/check-assets.mjs` checks only the limit per file.

## Proposal

- **Give the client the two facts without the history:**
  - the newest version;
  - for each patch, its version and the card ids it added, which is all `ribbon.ts` reads.
- **How:** a small Vite plugin that reads `patches.json` at build time and serves a virtual module, registered in `apps/web/vite.config.ts` and `apps/web/vitest.config.ts` alike. A file generated beside the wire files was rejected: it would need its own check to stay in step with `patches ship`.
- **`CATALOG_VERSION` keeps its value.** A test holds it to the engine module's `catalogVersion()`.
- **A test over the built site.** The entry script and the files it preloads hold no patch history and stay under a named compressed size.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/wire/cards.ts`, `apps/web/src/patches/ribbon.ts`
- `apps/web/vite.config.ts`, `apps/web/vitest.config.ts`
- A test beside `apps/web/src/net/check-assets.test.ts`, which already reads the built `dist`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No non-test module under `apps/web/src` imports `patches.json` statically. Only `source.ts`'s lazy glob loads it, and a test checks this.
- [ ] A test shows `CATALOG_VERSION` equals the wasm module's `catalogVersion()`.
- [ ] `ribbon.test.tsx` passes unchanged.
- [ ] A test over `dist`: the entry chunk and its preloads contain no patch-notes text, and their gzipped size is under a named constant.
- [ ] The Patch notes page still lists every patch.

## Size and risks

Small: 5 or 6 files in `apps/web`. Difficulty medium.

- The plugin must behave the same under `vite build`, `vite dev` and vitest.
- Parts of `apps/web/src/wire/` are rewritten by `cargo test`, so the new module must not sit where that happens.

---
Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it.

Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42695817116)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

First page loads stop downloading the patch history. `apps/web/src/wire/cards.ts` and `apps/web/src/patches/ribbon.ts` get the two facts they actually read — the newest version and each patch's added card ids — from a small Vite virtual module built from `crates/cards/patches/patches.json` at build time, instead of statically importing the 650 KB file. `CATALOG_VERSION` keeps its value, `ribbon.test.tsx` passes unchanged, the Patch notes page still lists every patch, and a new test holds the entry chunk plus its preloads free of patch-notes text and under a named gzipped size. Governing spec: §5.1 (patch data), §9.4 (versioned catalog shipped with the client).

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/patch-meta.ts` | new | `patchMeta()` plugin factory; module id `virtual:jackioh-patch-meta`; exports `PATCH_VERSION: string`, `PATCH_ADDED: readonly { readonly version: string; readonly added: readonly string[] }[]`. Lives here, not under `src/wire/`, because cargo tests rewrite `src/wire/generated/*`, `engineConfig.ts`, `serverConfig.ts`. |
| `apps/web/src/patch-meta.d.ts` | new | `declare module "virtual:jackioh-patch-meta"` with the two export types, so `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` passes. |
| `apps/web/src/wire/cards.ts` | change | Drop the `patches.json` import and `newestVersion()`; `export const CATALOG_VERSION: string = PATCH_VERSION` from the virtual module. `CATALOG`, aliases, `currentVersionName`/`versionNameFrom` untouched. |
| `apps/web/src/patches/ribbon.ts` | change | Drop the `patches.json` import; build `PATCH_LOG` by mapping `PATCH_ADDED` to `RibbonPatch` (`changes: added.map((id) => ({ id, kind: "added" as const }))`). `RibbonPatch`, `NEW_RIBBON_PATCHES`, `ribbonSet`, `NEW_RIBBON_SET` untouched. |
| `apps/web/vite.config.ts` | change | `import { patchMeta } from "./patch-meta.ts"`; `plugins: [react(), patchMeta(), staticPages()]`. |
| `apps/web/vitest.config.ts` | change | Same import; `plugins: [react(), patchMeta()]`. |
| `e2e/cypress.config.ts` | change | Same import; component `devServer.viteConfig.plugins` becomes `[react(), patchMeta()]` (component specs import `@jackioh/cards` through that server, which does not use `apps/web/vite.config.ts`). Update the "one plugin" comment. |
| `apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts` | new | Static-import scan; `dist` probes; `FIRST_LOAD_GZIP_BUDGET_BYTES`. |

Must not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`; `crates/`; `apps/web/src/patches/source.ts` (the lazy glob stays the only history loader); `ribbon.test.tsx`, `currentCatalog.test.ts` (kept, not edited); no `scripts/ci-scope.sh` change (new paths default to `web`/`e2e` on; `virtual:` literals are ignored by its scan); no `docs/v0.3.0/SURFACE.md` change (the `@jackioh/cards` exports table stays accurate); no ruling note (no game-rule decision, so no `spec check` impact).

## Steps

1. Create `apps/web/patch-meta.ts`. Copy the plugin shape from `apps/web/static-pages.ts` (`import type { Plugin } from "vite"`). Export `const PATCH_META_MODULE = "virtual:jackioh-patch-meta"` and `export function patchMeta(): Plugin` returning `{ name: "jackioh-patch-meta", resolveId(source) { return source === PATCH_META_MODULE ? "\0" + PATCH_META_MODULE : null; }, load(id) { ... } }`. `load` returns `null` unless `id === "\0" + PATCH_META_MODULE`; otherwise it `readFileSync(new URL("../../crates/cards/patches/patches.json", import.meta.url), "utf8")`, throws naming that path when the value is not an array or the last entry has no string `version`, and returns `` `export const PATCH_VERSION = ${JSON.stringify(version)};\nexport const PATCH_ADDED = ${JSON.stringify(patches.map((p) => ({ version: p.version, added: p.changes.filter((c) => c.kind === "added").map((c) => c.id) })))};\n` ``.
2. Create `apps/web/src/patch-meta.d.ts` declaring the module and the exact two export types from the table above.
3. Edit `apps/web/src/wire/cards.ts`: replace lines 6 and 15–24 (the `patchesJson` import and `newestVersion`) with `import { PATCH_VERSION } from "virtual:jackioh-patch-meta";` and `export const CATALOG_VERSION: string = PATCH_VERSION;`, keeping the `§9.4; R388` comment on the constant.
4. Edit `apps/web/src/patches/ribbon.ts`: replace line 6 with `import { PATCH_ADDED } from "virtual:jackioh-patch-meta";`, replace line 19 with the mapped `PATCH_LOG` from the table, and update the two comments that say the history is `patches.json` to say it is the slim per-patch added-ids list the plugin derives from it.
5. Register the plugin in `apps/web/vite.config.ts`, `apps/web/vitest.config.ts`, and `e2e/cypress.config.ts` exactly as the table says.
6. Create `apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts` (copy the `WEB`/`BUILT`/`existsSync`/`describe.skipIf` and `node:zlib` usage pattern from `check-assets.test.ts`):
   - `it("no non-test module imports patches.json statically")`: walk `apps/web/src`, skip `*.test.ts?(x)` and `src/test/`, fail on `from "…patches/patches.json"` or `import("…patches/patches.json")` in any remaining `.ts/.tsx`; plus `expect(readFileSync(source.ts)).toContain("import.meta.glob")`.
   - `describe.skipIf(!existsSync(BUILT))("first load")`: parse `dist/index.html` for the `type="module"` script `src` (fail if none) and every `rel="modulepreload"` `href`; read those files under `dist`.
   - Probes, sampled at test time from `crates/cards/patches/patches.json` (never card names — `catalog.json` shares those): first entry's `notes`, last entry's `notes`, last entry's `player.title`; assert each is a non-empty string and absent from every entry/preload file.
   - `expect(gzipSync(Buffer.concat(files)).length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(FIRST_LOAD_GZIP_BUDGET_BYTES)`.
7. Build once (`pnpm --dir apps/web build`), compute the gzipped total of the entry plus its preloads with a `node -e "zlib/readFileSync"` one-liner over `dist/index.html`, set `FIRST_LOAD_GZIP_BUDGET_BYTES` to that total rounded up to the next multiple of 8192, and re-run the new test with `dist` present so the skipped half executes.
8. Run typecheck, eslint on the touched files, and the Tests below. `cargo` suites are unaffected (no Rust changes).

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts` (new): static-scan test; `dist` probes test; gzip-budget test. Command: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/net/first-load.test.ts` (run again after step 7 with `dist` built).
- `apps/web/src/patches/ribbon.test.tsx` (unchanged): proves the ribbon still works on the slim log. Command: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/patches/ribbon.test.tsx`.
- `apps/web/src/game/currentCatalog.test.ts` (unchanged, lines 27–34 already assert `snapshot.version` is both `catalogVersion()` and `CATALOG_VERSION`): proves criterion 2. Command: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/game/currentCatalog.test.ts`.
- `apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx` (unchanged): proves the Patch notes page still lists every patch. Command: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/patches/PatchNotes.test.tsx`.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`; eslint over the eight touched files.

## Done when

- [ ] No non-test module under `apps/web/src` statically imports `patches.json` (scan test green); only `source.ts`'s lazy glob loads it.
- [ ] `currentCatalog.test.ts` green: `CATALOG_VERSION` equals the wasm module's `catalogVersion()`.
- [ ] `ribbon.test.tsx` green unchanged.
- [ ] `first-load.test.ts` green with `dist` present: entry plus preloads contain none of the three probe strings and fit `FIRST_LOAD_GZIP_BUDGET_BYTES`.
- [ ] `PatchNotes.test.tsx` green: the Patch notes page still lists every patch.
- [ ] `typecheck` and eslint on touched files green; `vite build`, `vitest`, and Cypress component runs share the one plugin (no `src/wire/` additions).

## Risks

- The slim log drops `changed`/`removed` entries, names, notes, and prose. Only `ribbonSet` reads `PATCH_LOG`, and only for `kind === "added"`, so nothing observable changes; the full history still loads lazily for the Patch notes page.
- After `patches ship`, a running `vite dev` serves the previous list until restart (`load` runs once per process); builds and tests always read the file fresh. No generated file means nothing can drift.
- `PATCH_ADDED` adds roughly 6 KB gzipped to every client chunk graph; the budget test holds the total.
- The Cypress component server needs the same plugin; without step 5's third registration, component specs importing `@jackioh/cards` fail to resolve the virtual module.

## Open questions

None. The only judgment call — slim shape versus full slimmed entries — is settled above: added ids only, because that is all `ribbon.ts` reads.
```
